title: Reported full back-pay can follow worker exit and alternative-employment search without proving durable recovery
source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release and Federal Circuit Court reasons, Fair Work Ombudsman v Longridge Group Pty Ltd [2015] FCCA 129

observations.period: 2011–2013; 59-year-old sales worker underpayment, resignation, alternative employment, and May 2013 payment

denominator.unit: one of two publicly described workers in the Longridge enforcement case; no population denominator

reported_shortfall.unit: Australian dollars before any source-specific adjustments

backpay.unit: court-reported gross remedy timing; worker-signed receipt and adequacy not retained

alternative_employment.unit: replacement-job quality and timing not observed

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman release and Federal Circuit Court reasons; worker-level underpayment, exit, alternative-employment response, enforcement, and reported payment are kept separate from later recovery.
observations.uncertainty: One case cannot estimate underpayment or remedy rates. The public record does not retain payment instruments, net or superannuation treatment, replacement-job quality, household effects, or later work and trust outcomes.
observations.subgroup: One 59-year-old sales worker with an advertised potential earning claim of at least A$120,000 who received commission-only payments below minimum entitlements.
observations.counterinterpretation: Court-recorded full back-pay can restore a formal wage entitlement while arriving after exit and alternative-employment search; it does not prove practical adequacy or durable security.

observations.period: 2011–2014; 32-year-old sales worker underpayment, resignation, alternative employment, and October 2014 payment

denominator.unit: one of two publicly described workers in the Longridge enforcement case; no population denominator

commission_paid.unit: Australian dollars during six months of employment

backpay.unit: court-reported gross remedy timing; worker-signed receipt and adequacy not retained

alternative_employment.unit: replacement-job quality and timing not observed

observations.method: Same official FWO and Federal Circuit Court extraction as the companion worker observation; the two workers are not pooled into a population estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The payment date is institutionally reported and the case does not provide independent bank confirmation, net/tax or superannuation treatment, adequacy, later livelihood, household, trust, recurrence, or exit outcomes.
observations.subgroup: One 32-year-old sales worker with real-estate and building qualifications who received no commission during six months of commission-only employment.
observations.counterinterpretation: A dated full-back-pay outcome can close the formal claim while leaving the worker's earlier income loss, employment transition, and practical recovery unresolved.

related_sources.claim: Official Fair Work Ombudsman enforcement release and reported penalty/back-pay context.
Federal Circuit Court reasons for worker-level amounts and payment dates.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the committed project ledger that retains the bounded official release and court-reasons extraction.
reproduction_audit.access_boundary: The public record reports full back-pay in installments but not worker-signed receipt, net amount, adequacy, later work, household recovery, trust, recurrence, or exit.

boundary: This record contains two separate public worker episodes from commission-only underpayment through resignation, alternative-employment pursuit, complaint, enforcement, and institutionally reported full back-pay. It does not establish independent receipt verification, adequacy, durable livelihood, prevalence, recurrence, trust change, collective action, or exit.
